summary: @cdnshell/loader ships an obfuscated remote-code loader that fetches and evals JavaScript at runtime
details: The package ships a single heavily obfuscated file (a1x4b4n8.js) whose behavior is to fetch JavaScript from a configurable remote base URL and execute it via `new Function(responseText)()`, plus decode and execute two ~10 KB embedded base64 blobs via `new Function(atob(...))()`, and install a 60-second `location.reload` interval. The file uses obfuscator.io-style string-array rotation (89-entry array, rotation count 0xdac59, custom-alphabet base64 + percent-URI decoder) and hex-mangled identifiers, with no source or build pairing shipped. The package's stated purpose is 'Static assets distribution', which does not require obfuscation, dynamic remote-code fetching, embedded base64 eval payloads, or a periodic page-reload timer. Any downstream page that references this loader executes attacker-controlled JavaScript pulled from the remote base URL together with the two obfuscated embedded payloads at bootstrap — the browser-skimmer/loader pattern using npm as the distribution channel.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
